messages:
cheng: Heads up — after landing fused-paged-flashx on canary, we see intermittent NaNs in logits on long sequences (~8k). Perf looks fine but accuracy drops on ~0.02% of requests.

lara: Can you paste repro and perf trace? Which dtype?

cheng: Repro: `./bench --model llama-7b --seq 8192 --kv paged --kernel fused-flashx --dtype fp16`
cheng: Logs:
```
E 2026-03-15 14:02:12 attention.cc:482 softmax: exp overflow -> inf
nan count: 12 / 50000 (0.024%)
kernel: fused-paged-flashx, gpu 4090, sm 8.6
attn-time: p50 4.9ms p95 6.7ms
```

ravi: @cheng thanks. Likely softmax exponent overflow for fp16 when logits get large. Are we doing per-block max subtraction? flashx used an lse-offset fallback before.

maya: We turned off the lse-offset fallback in the kernel selector to squeeze perf on 4k loads. Might be why it skipped the stable-softmax path.

jeff: Perf-bot trace: fused-flashx is ~1.8x faster than paged baseline at seq=4k but only ~1.1x at 8k. Memory jitter also increases.

cheng: Quick mitigation: enable kernel selector guard: if max(logits)-min(logits) > 30 then use stable-softmax-path. I patched locally and NaNs dropped to ~0.001%.

ops-bot: Rolling canary with kernel-guard enabled: rollout id rwd-2026-03-15-kguard, 5% traffic.

lara: Can we get perf cost delta? If fallback is frequent it'll kill p95.

ravi: Microbench: fallback adds ~0.9ms median and ~2.7ms p95 on 8k sequences; but it prevents correctness failures.

maya: Alternative: compute exp in fp32 accumulator for the softmax exponent and then cast back to fp16 — cheaper than doing full fallback maybe. Need to validate numeric and perf tradeoffs.

cheng: I'll open a PR with tests and a feature flag. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4281

jeff: Add unit test with synthetic extreme logits (range ~1e5) and a stress job with kv-coldstart + long sequences.

ravi: Also add telemetry: `softmax_overflow_count{kernel,dtype}` so we can measure per-kernel failure modes in prod.

lara: Good. Timeline?

cheng: PR by end of day, canary in ~2hrs, auto-revert threshold if p95 impact > 10%.

jeff: :thumbsup:

perf-bot: NOTE: rollback triggered at 1719876568 by auto-sla because p95 increased 12% in canary.

cheng: Reverting while we iterate on a clip/scale approach.

maya: Next step: try max-subtract + dynamic float-scaling (shift by exponent) inside the kernel; should be a microcost compared to full fallback.

ravi: I'll prototype an exp-stable path in the fused kernel and run microbench.

cheng: Thanks all. I'll paste follow-up perf numbers tomorrow.
